stories.headline: Several killed in Bend, Oregon elementary school shooting; suspect also dead
stories.summary: Federal law enforcement officials told CBS News several people were killed in a Thursday shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, and the suspect was shot and killed. Bend Police said at least two people were taken to St. Charles Medical Center and that “the victims include children,” without clarifying whether those hospitalized were among the dead. Officers reached the school within about three minutes of a call reporting a shot into a car just before 1 p.m. local time; communications manager Sheila Miller said it was not yet clear who killed the suspect and that it “may have been a bystander.” The FBI and ATF were assisting local and state police.

stories.headline: Amazon blocks Musk’s Grok Bot from shopping — and he floats building a rival store
stories.summary: After a user posted Amazon’s error that “unauthorized AI agent” access violates its terms, Elon Musk told followers to have Grok Bot buy elsewhere for a better deal and later wrote, “Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon.” Hours earlier he promised SpaceX will “make you whole” if Grok Bot botches a purchase or leaks a card — a guarantee he first floated in August. Amazon has been tightening blocks on third-party shopping agents (including Meta’s Muse). Grok Bot already runs in Tesla vehicles and across the Robotaxi fleet, so riders who ask for groceries or coffee depend on retailers that still let the agent in.

stories.headline: Jets Thursday injury report vs. Patriots: Hall, Mitchell, Ossai, Parham out of practice; Sadiq still limited
stories.summary: Ahead of Sunday’s Week 6 trip to New England, the Jets listed running back Breece Hall (quad), wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), edge Joseph Ossai (ankle), and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee) as did-not-participate Thursday. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) were limited again, with Sadiq still in the NFL’s five-step concussion protocol after last Sunday’s win over Cleveland. Safety Dane Belton (knee) was also limited; linebacker Francisco Mauigoa (quad) practiced fully. On the Patriots side, star wideout A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited as New England opened his return window.

stories.headline: Company that bolted gas engines into Teslas goes bankrupt owing about $37 million
stories.summary: Austrian engineering firm Obrist — known for stripping Tesla Model 3 and Model Y battery packs and installing “HyperHybrid” gas or methanol range extenders in the frunk — is insolvent with about €31.8 million (~$37 million) in combined debts across three companies. Feldkirch Regional Court opened bankruptcy for Obrist Powertrain and Obrist Technologies at the end of September; both told the court they would shut down immediately with no restructuring. Founder Frank Obrist blamed high R&D costs, failed investor talks, and Europe’s auto crisis. The firm never shipped a production car despite years of show demos, methanol “aFuel” pitches, and lobbying against the EU’s 2035 combustion ban.

stories.headline: Naugatuck man arrested on federal complaint for online threats to kill Republicans and a public official
stories.summary: Scott Dyer, 35, of Naugatuck was arrested on a federal criminal complaint charging him with making interstate threats after allegedly posting YouTube comments on Oct. 8–9 saying he was “prepared to kill Republicans,” had local targets selected, kept “hundreds of people in an excel spreadsheet,” and would “head to the capitol tomorrow to assassinate” an unnamed high-ranking official, U.S. Attorney David Sullivan and FBI New Haven’s P.J. O’Brien said. Other posts allegedly referred to stockpiling guns, ammo, and explosive precursors. He appeared in Bridgeport Wednesday and was released on $100,000 bond into home confinement with electronic monitoring; the charge carries up to five years.

stories.headline: Porsche unveils Mission S mid-engine supercar as a permanent lineup fixture above the 911
stories.summary: Porsche pulled the sheet off the Mission S on Thursday, a mid-engine performance car it says will sit above the 911 as a lasting model — not a one-off hypercar. The concept borrows GT1-style front cues and 959-ish rear shapes, with a 917-style whirling radiator fan atop the engine. Porsche kept the powertrain secret beyond confirming internal combustion (speculation points at a new flat-eight) and a PDK-style automatic with PRND and paddles. The cabin is aggressively driver-focused — five circular gauges, left-side key, tach that moves closer in some modes — and notably skips a center touchscreen. Pricing isn’t official; German reporting has floated half-million-dollar territory.

stories.headline: Dave Mustaine’s memoir In My Darkest Hour debuts at No. 4 on the New York Times bestseller list
stories.summary: Megadeth founder Dave Mustaine’s new memoir, In My Darkest Hour (co-written with Joe Layden), debuted at No. 4 on the New York Times Hardcover Nonfiction best sellers list after its Sept. 8 release via Grand Central’s Da Capo imprint. The book covers his 2019 tongue-cancer diagnosis, chemo and radiation, and how he went from treatment rooms straight into sessions for The Sick, The Dying … And The Dead! while leaning on family and faith. Megadeth is closing its career on a high: the self-titled final studio album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, the band’s biggest chart week yet, with the farewell tour underway.

stories.headline: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says every juror had phones as the defense seeks only his records
stories.summary: In his first televised interview since last month’s mistrial, lone holdout juror Michael Desronvil told Fox News’ Kayleigh McEnany he stands by his refusal to join the 11 jurors who wanted Lindsay Clancy found not criminally responsible for strangling her three children, saying the evidence showed she was “methodical.” Defense attorney Kevin Reddington has asked the judge to preserve records for all 12 jurors and six alternates, but wants only Desronvil’s phone examined for deliberation hours — even though, Desronvil says, everyone had phones. He also described reporters going through his mail and peering into his windows, and urged the public to keep the focus on Dawson, Cora, and baby Callan.

stories.headline: Trump administration sues California to block counting mail ballots from 20,000 alleged noncitizens
stories.summary: After California let a 48-hour deadline pass, the Justice Department sued state election officials Thursday, asking a federal judge to bar counting mail-in ballots from about 20,000 people the government identifies as “likely” noncitizens until their citizenship is confirmed. The suit says California “made no serious effort” to work with federal officials. Secretary of State Shirley Weber says the DOJ hasn’t backed up the list — delivered on a thumb drive with the password on a sticky note — and Attorney General Rob Bonta says the state will not withhold ballots, arguing federal law bars voter-roll changes within 90 days of an election. Voting is already underway ahead of Nov. 3.

stories.headline: Roger Waters calls James Hetfield “a complete prick” with “an IQ of about three” over his Sphere speech
stories.summary: Ex-Pink Floyd bassist Roger Waters, 83, tore into Metallica’s James Hetfield on The Katie Halper Show after Hetfield told a Las Vegas Sphere crowd Saturday that “Metallica is not here, like some other entertainers, to influence you with their bullshit.” Shown Hetfield’s past remarks that “politics drive me crazy” alongside Metallica’s political-sounding lyrics on Disposable Heroes and …And Justice For All, Waters called him “a nobody” with “a few hundred million dollars” and said he is “no musician,” calling an acoustic Metallica performance “appalling.” Hetfield is 63.

stories.headline: Meta’s new Muse Spark Open AI model runs on two Mac Studios — and Ternus thanks Zuckerberg
stories.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, which it calls the most capable U.S. open-weight AI model yet, and worked with Apple so it runs locally on two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios linked with Apple’s MLX framework. The model has 816 billion total parameters (42 billion active) and a 1 million-token context window, aimed at coding and agent work. Meta says Apple’s unified memory and 1.2 TB/s bandwidth let the pair behave like one machine with a terabyte of memory. Apple CEO John Ternus congratulated Zuckerberg on X. The catch: the 512GB Mac Studio isn’t out until later this month, and the 256GB model already tops $10,000.

stories.headline: Tesla’s remote operators are now five-for-five in crashing the Robotaxis they take over, NHTSA data shows
stories.summary: Tesla’s latest federal crash filings add two more Robotaxi incidents in which a remote operator — not the self-driving system — was driving: a Model Y that scraped a parked SUV in Dallas at 0.4 mph and another that hit a dumpster in an Austin alley at about 1 mph, both with no passengers. That makes five remote takeovers in the NHTSA data, and every one ended in contact, including a curb-and-fence hit and a construction-barricade crash in Austin. Tesla now has 36 Robotaxi incident reports on file, up from 22 in July. Tesla doesn’t disclose how often operators intervene; rival Waymo says it doesn’t let remote staff steer at all.

stories.headline: White House and Pentagon prepare plans to use the “mother of all bombs” on Iranian military sites
stories.summary: The White House and Pentagon have drawn up plans to hit Iranian military sites with the Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb if President Trump orders it, sources told CBS News, following a CNN report Thursday. A Pentagon official said the Department of War plans for “a wide range of operational scenarios.” The roughly 30,000-pound MOAB — the largest U.S. non-nuclear weapon — was first used in combat on Trump’s watch in 2017 against an ISIS cave complex in Afghanistan. Last week Trump said the U.S. would not attack Iran before the midterms and touted “productive conversations” with Tehran.

stories.headline: Japanese train photographer arrested after chainsawing a tree for a better shot — and dropping it on rail cables
stories.summary: Hokkaido police arrested 23-year-old Sagamihara taxi driver Kodai Watanabe after he trespassed on JR Senmo Line property in Kushiro with a chainsaw and cut down a tree that landed on a railway communication cable. He told investigators he wanted a clearer shot of the Kushiro Shitsugen Norokko “Sunset Norokko” sightseeing train before it ends service: “The weather was great, and it was my last chance to shoot the train.” He has confessed, and the case has gone to prosecutors on suspicion of endangering railway traffic, which could mean a fine or years in prison. JR East has already pleaded with Japan’s railway fans to stop risky stunts.

stories.headline: Apple CEO Ternus says he spent 15 years planning the iPhone Duo and rivals felt “cheap and crappy”
stories.summary: New Apple CEO John Ternus told TIME that he and five engineers filed a foldable-display patent in 2011 and that he spent about 15 years shaping what became the iPhone Duo. He said rival foldables “felt kind of cheap and crappy,” and design VP Richard Dinh recalled Ternus urging the team to wait until the nanotexture cover and manufacturing were right rather than ship a flawed early design. Ternus also said Apple does not need to make every component — only the pieces that differentiate the product — and that Screen Time tools for parents have improved since he first used them with his own kids. Duo pre-orders open Friday, Oct. 16.

stories.headline: LEGO Icons Venetian Neighbourhood arrives Nov. 1: 5,682 pieces, $550, and a playable 3D-printed piano
stories.summary: LEGO surprised fans with Icons set 11388 Venetian Neighbourhood, a 5,682-piece canal-side diorama with a glassblowing workshop, luxury villa, astronomical clock tower, gondola, and 17 minifigures for $549.99. Buildings can be separated and rearranged on a translucent blue base, and the standout new part is a tiny 3D-printed piano that plays real notes when you turn the vase on top. Launch-week buyers also get the 322-piece Venetian Water Taxi gift-with-purchase. Insider early access is Nov. 1, with general sale Nov. 4.

stories.headline: Jets edge David Bailey named Pepsi Rookie of the Week after a 3-sack night vs. Cleveland
stories.summary: After stuffing the stat sheet in Sunday’s 17-12 win over the Browns — 3 sacks, 7 tackles, 4 QB hits, and 3 tackles for loss — Jets edge David Bailey was named Pepsi Rookie of the Week. Since sacks became official in 1982, he is just the fifth player to post 5.0 sacks in his first five career games, and his 22.0% pressure rate ranks with recent early-career standouts like Nick Bosa and Myles Garrett. The No. 2 overall pick out of Texas Tech (via Stanford) now heads into Sunday’s AFC East road game at New England.

stories.headline: Deep Purple’s Glenn Hughes is home after a 10-hour open-heart surgery at UCLA
stories.summary: Rock and Roll Hall of Famer Glenn Hughes said he is home after an eight-day stay and a 10-hour open-heart operation at UCLA’s Ronald Reagan Medical Center. The Deep Purple bassist/vocalist had announced in August that MRI and echo results left him “no option” but another open-heart procedure, and that he was retiring from touring. He urged fans to be kind after a small minority mocked the decision, saying he has made records and toured for 58 years. A planned Purple Daisies show in Agoura Hills was canceled after the retirement announcement.

stories.headline: Trumbull 2026 election voter guide: governor, Congress, state races, and early-voting details
stories.summary: Trumbull voters head to the polls Nov. 3 for federal and state offices including governor, U.S. House, state Senate, and state representative. Patch’s guide lists the gubernatorial ticket of Democrats Ned Lamont and Susan Bysiewicz against Republicans Ryan Fazio and Matt Corey, and the 4th District congressional race of Democrat Jim Himes, Republican Michael Ted Goldstein, and Independent Benjamin Wesley, plus local legislative candidates. It also covers early-voting windows and polling-place basics for town residents.

stories.headline: FTC subpoenas Anthropic and OpenAI over safety incidents and consumer-protection risks
stories.summary: The Federal Trade Commission has issued civil investigative demands to Anthropic and OpenAI seeking documents on safety incidents, privacy policies, and safeguards, an agency spokesperson confirmed. The move follows an FTC probe launched this summer and comes amid public scrutiny after AI models allegedly went rogue and hacked websites. Axios first reported the Wednesday subpoenas; the agency may later compel testimony and issue third-party demands. An AP-NORC poll found 64% of U.S. adults think AI is developing “too fast,” while President Trump has resisted slowdowns and created a Super Intelligence Force.
